search_scope: Limited primary-source search for exponential-twisting failure, mixture importance-sampling repair, conditional simulation, and learning-before-sampling costs. No exhaustive priority search.

sources.title: Counterexamples in importance sampling for large deviations probabilities
sources.verification: Primary author-hosted paper opened; abstract and paper text inspected.
sources.relation: Closest conceptual predecessor for poor or infinite variance from an exponential change of measure and accounting for multiple ways a rare event occurs.

sources.authors: Tim J. Brereton; Joshua C. C. Chan; Dirk P. Kroese
sources.title: Fitting mixture importance sampling distributions via improved cross-entropy
sources.verification: Primary UQ-hosted full paper opened; sections 2-4 inspected.
sources.relation: Exponential-twisting failure, disjoint-cause decomposition, state-dependent proposals, and mixture repair. Its proposal families are not restricted to the bounded scalar-T Esscher family excluded here.

sources.authors: Hock Peng Chan; Tze Leung Lai
sources.title: Efficient importance sampling for Monte Carlo evaluation of exceedance probabilities
sources.verification: Author preprint abstract and journal metadata opened.
sources.relation: Suitable mixtures of exponentially twisted measures can be asymptotically optimal in other models; distinguishes those results from the specific all-scalar-mixtures obstruction.

sources.title: Improved algorithms for rare event simulation with heavy tails
sources.verification: Author publication-list entry and university publication metadata inspected; abstract-level comparison only.
sources.relation: Conditional Monte Carlo and component-focused importance sampling in a distinct heavy-tailed sums model.

sources.title: Efficient importance sampling under partial information
sources.verification: Primary author-hosted full paper opened; sections 1-3 inspected.
sources.relation: Explicit learning-versus-sampling resource allocation in an unknown-function model; does not itself prove the present rare-branch obstruction.
